reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling NVA4 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, which ranks 22nd of the 25 Virginia data centers with disclosed figures and amounts to 0.7% of the state's published 1,603 MW.

The pattern here is disclosure, not scale. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities and only 25 publish capacity numbers, so any ranking built on them describes a small, self-selected slice of the market. NVA4's 128,715 square feet of technical space against 11 MW works out to a modest power density, and the implied count of roughly 275 racks at 40 kW per rack is an assumption about AI training density, not a published fact. The facility lists no certifications.

For AI specifically, this is a small existing asset in the country's most consolidated data center market. It sits outside the tier of facilities whose power draw shapes near-term scaling constraints in Virginia. Nothing in the data connects it to a specific training cluster, customer, or grid interconnection.

What the data does not cover is the part that would matter most: grid supply, interconnection queue position, and operator plans to expand or add power. The suitability score of 57 is a weighted mean of published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing. Treat the ranking as a statement about who reports, not about who is large.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
